solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guy gets brother involved in 'domestic' …

indicators.note: the brother is wrapped up inside the word for domestic, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: domestic means to do with the home

explanation.surface: A man finds his brother caught up in a household row, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like a row between partners, but here it simply means home.
explanation.definitionFit: Hombre is Spanish-derived slang for a man or fellow, a synonym for guy.

clue.text: See 18
Prodigy, currently growing up in Derby, trained with zero input

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters being drilled into a new order

parts.note: an input of zero adds the round letter O to the mix

indicators.note: in a down clue, growing up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: currently means now, at the present time

explanation.surface: A precocious child is being raised and schooled in Derby, an English Midlands city, with no outside help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing up' seems to describe the prodigy, but reverses NOW to WON in a down clue; setter-wise WON sits whole inside BOYDER, the letters of Derby plus O that 'trained' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy wonder is a remarkably gifted young man, the very picture of a prodigy.

clue.text: Former husband on drink? Blow!

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone learns their former husband has hit the bottle and swears in exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow!' reads as a mild curse, but it is the instruction to breathe out.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe air out of the lungs is to blow it out, a direct synonym.

clue.text: … it may be about his present computer image: 'Gin-soaked Wife'

definitions.text: it may be about his present

parts.note: a GIF is a common computer image file format

indicators.note: being soaked in gin means the wife sits surrounded by the gin

parts.note: a gin is a trap for catching game

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a man's gift turns out to be a picture of his wife drunk on gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin here is not the spirit but a snare, TRAP, with W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gift-wrap is decorative paper that goes around a present, so it is what surrounds the man's gift.

clue.text: Dead from flatulence — that's novel!

parts.note: someone dead is said to be gone
to suffer from wind is to be with the wind, wind meaning flatulence

explanation.surface: A comic cause of death, gas, is declared to be quite original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the definition: Margaret Mitchell's famous book.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone with the Wind is Margaret Mitchell's 1936 novel of the American Civil War.

clue.text: Among the running deer he may gain a speedy advantage

definitions.text: Among the running deer he may gain a speedy advantage

parts.words: Among the running deer he may gain a speedy advantage
parts.note: a quick stag among a running herd would be a fast male deer, and that same phrase means money made quickly and easily

explanation.surface: A stag outruns the herd and gets ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast buck is easily and quickly made money, a speedy gain, while a buck is also a male deer.

clue.text: Isle of Man?

parts.note: the Isle of Man is a real island; the other island off England's south coast is named with an old word for a person or man

explanation.definitionFit: Wight is an archaic word for a person, and the Isle of Wight is an English island, so it is literally an isle of man.

clue.text: Material irritated poodle's paw — no suggestion of soreness

indicators.note: irritated suggests the letters stirred up into a new order
no means the letter is left out of the fodder
a mere suggestion of the word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dog's paw is inflamed, but it doesn't seem sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no suggestion of soreness' drops the S from POODLESPAW; the remaining POODLEPAW is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Applewood is the timber of the apple tree, a material used for smoking food and woodturning.

clue.text: Married a New York tenor initially — Henry's son? You shouldn't have!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of tenor

parts.note: Hank is a pet form of Henry, so a son of Hank is Hanks, as in surnames formed from fathers' names

explanation.surface: A wedding announcement listing a bride, New York and a tenor, with a nod to Henry's son.
explanation.walkthrough: Surnames ending in -s often mean 'son of', so Henry's son is HANKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you shouldn't have is a polite expression of gratitude for a gift.

clue.text: Grow apart from grand primate

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Someone drifts away from a grand old primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grow apart' sounds like estrangement but means to open wide.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open or split wide, as a wound or seam that comes apart.

clue.text: Pope's digested pronouncements mentioning knowledge of guns?

indicators.note: mentioning means saying out loud, so the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: the lore of cannon is knowledge of big guns

explanation.surface: A pope's rulings unexpectedly reference artillery expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where lore and law sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Canon law is the codified body of rules issued by Church authority, including papal decrees.

clue.text: See 24
Women having a way with patients

parts.note: RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: A woman has a fine bedside manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a way with patients' reads as a nurse's knack, but way is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital room's occupants can be referred to collectively, as when the whole ward is fed.

clue.text: Discover a crime without trace, unusually …

indicators.note: without means outside, so the crime goes around the other letters

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of trace are set in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone uncovers a crime that oddly left no trace, the ellipsis leading on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside; 'unusually' rearranges the letters of trace to CERTA.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, a synonym of discover.

clue.text: Friar's jaunt into candy store

parts.note: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion, so Friar's gives the name with its possessive S
a hop is a short trip, a jaunt

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's friar makes a quick trip into a sweet shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck shop is a British school shop selling snacks and sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck shop sells sweets and snacks, especially at a British school, so it is a kind of candy store.

clue.text: … turning up misdemeanour in exclusive Middle East setting, celebrate

parts.note: sole means exclusive, belonging to one alone

indicators.note: the Middle East letters form a setting around the other piece
in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sin is a misdemeanour

explanation.surface: Continuing on, a wrongdoing surfaces in an exclusive Middle Eastern venue, yet people celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' sounds like appearing, but reverses SIN to NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To solemnise is to celebrate a ceremony, especially a marriage, formally.

clue.text: Georgia's wearing changed style in glee — such revelatory attire!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wear the Georgia letters, which sit inside them
changed style signals the letters being rearranged

parts.note: GE is the country code for Georgia; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Georgia gleefully wears a revealing new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia is the country, code GE, not the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a sheer, often revealing, nightgown, so the attire reveals a lot.

clue.text: At heart, Carol's worried for her in 5

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: Carol is anxious at heart about some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At heart' looks like a pick of middle letters, but its letters are part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine of Gone with the Wind, the novel at 5 down.

clue.text: Game of pool I dropped out of — you, we hear, substituted?

indicators.note: the letter I leaves the word for pool
substituted shows a new letter takes the dropped one's place

parts.note: a lido is an open-air swimming pool

indicators.note: we hear signals a word judged by sound

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone quits a pool game and you take their place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: For that reason, first European's dropped ultimatum

indicators.note: dropped means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: thereat is an old word meaning for that reason

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word European, which is also its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Because a leading European pulled out, someone issues an ultimatum.
explanation.walkthrough: THEREAT is formal or archaic English for 'on that account'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a final demand backed by a threat of consequences.

clue.text: Fasten in place and push!

indicators.note: the fastening word goes inside the abbreviation for place

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, in addresses
to rope something is to fasten it

explanation.surface: Instructions: secure something, then shove it.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to drive or push forward.

clue.text: Pull a pint regularly in Barnet?

indicators.note: regularly signals taking every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Pouring pints regularly in Barnet, a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but also rhyming slang: Barnet Fair means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait is a braid found in hair, which Cockney rhyming slang calls the barnet.

clue.text: Disc with edge half-destroyed — these things don't last

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record, a disc
a hem is an edge of cloth

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: erased means wiped out, destroyed

explanation.surface: A record with a damaged rim.
explanation.walkthrough: ERASED is cut to its first half, ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are short-lived items, things that are fleeting or transitory.

clue.text: Letter Ruth redirected about book for him in 5

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the book letter
redirected suggests a letter sent along a different route, so its letters go a new way

explanation.surface: A letter for Ruth is sent to a new address, concerning a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhett Butler is the hero of Gone with the Wind, the novel at 5 down.

clue.text: Farewell from Lancashire estate in 5

definitions.meaning: ... is a northern English goodbye, used in Lancashire
the O'Hara family plantation in Gone with the Wind is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ra is northern English slang for goodbye, and Tara is the plantation in Gone with the Wind.

clue.text: Manual trades' criteria?

parts.note: a manual is a guide
trades are lines of business

explanation.surface: Standards set by manual trades such as plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual' reads as hands-on work, but is a handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidelines are principles or standards to follow, criteria for action.

clue.text: Don't need to get involved in a row

indicators.note: getting involved suggests letters tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to stay out of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a row' looks like a quarrel but is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: End-to-end describes things placed one after another, in a line.

clue.text: Contract Jobcentre at Yeovil — do it!

indicators.note: do it urges the solver to carry out the extraction from inside the words

explanation.surface: Urging someone to sign up at the Yeovil job centre, Yeovil being a town in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between parties, a kind of contract.
